title.narrative: OECD/Paris21 and SCB Partnership- Statistic Systems Capacity Development
OECD/Paris21 and SCB Partnership- Statistical Systems Capacity Development

description.narrative:
OECD/PARIS21 and Statistic Sweden, a specialist Swedish authority, have applied for funding of approximately SEK 40 000 000 to jointly carry out the “Global program to develop capacity in data and statistics for the 2030 Agenda” during the period 2019-2022.
The overall objectives for the intervention are:
1.Low and middle income countries have the possibility and capacity to participate in global dialogue and follow up on the 2030 Agenda.
2.Inclusive partnership established, including low and middle income countries, that contribute to improving the use of data and statistics in the follow-up and global implementation of the 2030-Agenda.
The specific objective for the development intervention is:
- Improved quality availability and use of data and indicators in following up on the implementation of the 2030 Agenda.
In order to achieve the specific objective, the partners will work together over the next four years towards the following intermediate outcomes:
-Improved knowledge and capacity among data users and producers. -Improved global/regional dialogue and mutual learning across national statistical systems and the data ecosystem for better coordination and increased data use/demand. -Increased capacity at national level to reduce data gaps and produce quality statistics through agile data planning processes.
The intervention is in line with PARIS21 Program of Work, which has a total annual budget of approximately 5 MEURO. The largest donors are DIFID, Switzerland and Canada. The Swedish contribution to OECD/PARIS 21 is approximately 6 MSEK over a four-year period, in total 24 MSEK. In addition, approximately 4 MSEK will annually be provided to Statistics Sweden, in total 16,4 MSEK. The total contribution is 40 400 000 SEK.

OECD/PARIS21 och SCB, en svensk myndighet med omfattade erfarenhet av bilateralt utvecklingsarbete inom statistik, har ansökt om finansiering på 40 miljoner kronor för att i partnerskap genomföra ett "Globalt program för att utveckla kapacitet i data och statistik för Agenda 2030" under perioden 2019-2022.
De övergripande målen för programmet är:
1. Låg- och medelinkomstländer har möjlighet och kapacitet att delta i global dialog och följa upp 2030-agendan.
2. Inkluderande partnerskap, inklusive låg- och medelinkomstländer, som bidrar till att förbättra användningen av data och statistik i uppföljningen och det globala genomförandet av 2030-agendan.
Det specifika målet för programmet är:
- Förbättrad tillgänglighet och användning av data och indikatorer för uppföljning av genomförandet av 2030-agendan.
För att uppnå det specifika målet ska parterna samarbeta mot följande resultat:
- Förbättrad kunskap och kapacitet bland användare av data och dataproducenter. - Förbättrad global/regional dialog och ömsesidigt lärande mellan nationella statistiska system och data-ekosystem för bättre samordning och ökad användning och efterfrågan av data. - Ökad kapacitet på nationell nivå för att minska datagap och producera statistik av hög kvalitet, genom agila dataplaneringsprocesser.
Programmet går i linje med PARIS21:s beslutade arbetsplan. Arbetsplanen har en total årlig budget på cirka 5 MEURO. De största givarna till OECD/PARIS21 är DIFID, Schweiz och Kanada.
Det svenska bidraget till OECD/PARIS21 är årligen cirka 6 MSEK över en fyraårsperiod, totalt 24 MSEK.
Utöver bidraget till OECD/PARIS21 kommer Sida att årligen avsätta cirka 4 MSEK för SCB som ska bidra till PARIS21 med sin specifika kompetens kring administrativa system/data, systematisk produktion av gender data, nationalräkenskaper och specifik kontextkunskap. SCB:s totala budget uppgår till 16,4 MSEK.
Den totala budgeten för denna insats uppgår till 40 400 000 SEK.

Statistics Sweden (SCB) and OECD (PARIS21) received financing from Sida to implement a joint intervention with the objective to "Improve quality, availability and use of data and indicators in following up the implementation of the 2030 Agenda". The project became fully harmonized with the PARIS21 strategy, which was adopted in 2021.
SCB provided technical support to PARIS21 in the implementation of the program, offering Swedish expertise in order to ensure partnerdriven and sustainable capacity development in statistics. In addition SCB collaborated with a number of organisations such as the United Nations Statistics Division, the International Office for Migration, and the African Union, to implement specific initiatives related to developing stable national statistics systems that highlight the needs of the population in order to eradicate poverty.
PARIS21 mission to "put robust data and statistics at the heart of decision making for inclusive sustainable development" steered the strategy´s three strategic pillars of change accelerate innovation, bridge data ecosystems and develop statistical capacity.
Five key outcomes has been identified to have the greatest impact on better data for better lives for all:
- National statistical systems are fit for purpose - Data use for policy-making is strengthened - Data ecosystems are equipped to leave no-one behind - More and better financing for development data is available - Partnerships for data-driven sustainable development are enhanced

title.narrative: Beslut om insats PARIS21 och SCB _ SDG Capacity Development

description.narrative:
The Paris21 Progress Report 2024 (which also constitutes the final report to Sida) was presented in April 2025. The report does not have a summary, but rather introductory "highlights". The report contains a number of hyperlinks which is good as Paris21 produces much reports/analysis etc. PARIS21 launched eight analytical reports in 2024, one Framework and Toolkit, and one E-learning course.
Examples of results year 2024:
- Expert voices came together at the PARIS21 Spring Meetings to tackle the subject of how to use AI for good. In partnership with the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund, the conference: Data and AI for Sustainable Development: Building a Smarter Future was held in the margins of the World Banks Spring Meetings.
- PARIS21 and UN Women's combined expertise developed a measurement of gender data capacity and analysed 83 countries to support countries, development partners and researchers to better understand where investments in gender data capacity are most needed and have the potential to be most effective. Furthermore, close collaboration to develop Gender Data Use case studies with longstanding PARIS21 partners Dominican Republic, Maldives, Rwanda and Kenya revealed how gender data are used, particularly in the context of policy making.
- PARIS21 developed a unique approach which provides a birds eye view of countries unique institutional and legal frameworks, network of climate change data producers and the various communities who rely on this data. The Climate Change Data Ecosystem Framework and Toolkit was launched in a regional event co-organised with Agence Nationale de la Statistique et de la Démographie (ANSD) Senegal and has been implemented by seven countries to date. Based on this work, a training program for civil society organisations (CSOs) to use climate change data in their advocacy efforts was implemented in two countries with another seven lined up for 2025.
The final report (December 2023) from SCB gives the following highlighted achievements towards three outcome areas:
1. National statistical systems are fit for purpose, in which: National Statistical Systems Human Resource policies and skills strengthened from engagement with 18 African countries.
For example the Zambian Environment Statistics was improved and it play's a crucial role as it visualizes the country's development challenges but also enables the government to follow up and measure progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
2. Data use in policymaking is strengthened with communication for the dissemination of gender-based statistics in Madagascar and Maldives was improved.
3. Data ecosystems are equipped to leave no one behind, with training in Gender Segregated Statistics in Rwanda in partnership with the Gender Monitoring Office in Rwanda and Rwanda's National Institute of Statistics (NISR).
Given the need to better understand the results of the program during the period when Sida provided funding to it (2019 - 2024), additional reports from Paris21/SCB, was presented in January 2026. These reports (2019 - 2024 PARIS21 & Sweden:Collaborating for Results and a "Results" report-table) gives a better understanding and account of results during the full funding period.
Here follows a few examples of results from the full program period:
- Outcome area 1: National statistical offices improved workforce planning, competency frameworks, leadership capacity, and staff retention strategies. HR managers benefited from baseline assessments, regional workshops and peer learning (e.g. Nairobi and Benin). Strengthened ability to recruit, retain and develop qualified staff enhanced sustainability and quality of official statistics.
- Outcome area 2: In countries supported by Statistics Sweden and PARIS21, the accessibility, visibility, and dissemination of official statistics were significantly improved. This led to greater use of statistics in national policy and planning documents, senior-level decision-making, and public discourse. For example, in the Maldives, parliamentary staff were trained to access, interpret, and apply census data, develop policy briefs, and communicate statistics effectively. The Maldives Bureau of Statistics, together with PARIS21 and Statistics Sweden, refined communication strategies, translated datasets into key messages and press releases, and improved dissemination of census results.
- Outcome area 3: Increased availability and use of gender-relevant and environment and climate-related statistics. In Caribbean SIDS (e.g. Grenada), PARIS21s ecosystem approach strengthened collaboration among NSOs, line ministries, civil society and other data actors to improve climate data coordination, sharing and use for adaptation policies.
- Outcome area 4 (indirect): Sustained visibility of statistics in international financing discussions and improved targeting of resources to priority countries and high need areas.
- Outcome area 5: Enhanced coordination, knowledge exchange, and complementarity among countries and international actors (e.g. OECD, GPEDC, UNECE, UN Women, IOM GMDAC). These partnerships reduced duplication, strengthened methodological development, and increased the effectiveness of support to partner countries.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
